title_en: The Scientific Giant Who Changed the World
english_paragraphs: On 29 May 1919, as a total eclipse obscured the sun, two British expeditions photographed stars in its apparent vicinity. Arthur Eddington observed from Príncipe, an island off West Africa; Crommelin and Davidson from Sobral, in north-eastern Brazil. They were testing general relativity's bold prediction that the sun's gravity would deflect starlight.

On 6 November, at a joint meeting of the Royal Society and the Royal Astronomical Society, the findings were hailed as confirming it. The Times proclaimed a "Revolution in Science"; a New York Times headline read "Lights All Askew in the Heavens". Almost overnight, Einstein, eminent among physicists, became a global celebrity.

Stockholm proved harder to dazzle. The Nobel physics committee valued rigorous experimental confirmation, and committee member Allvar Gullstrand, a Nobel-winning eye specialist, deemed the empirical support for relativity insufficient. Since no nomination fulfilled Nobel's criteria, the 1921 prize was reserved for a year, as the statutes permit.

On 9 November 1922 the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences conferred it on Einstein, citing his services to theoretical physics, especially his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect. That law, which governs how light ejects electrons from metal, helped underpin quantum theory. A letter the next day clarified that the prize took no account of relativity. Einstein, then aboard a steamer bound for Japan, would miss the December ceremony.

On 11 July 1923, in Gothenburg, Sweden, he delivered his Nobel lecture before a congress of Nordic scientists, devoting it to the fundamental ideas and problems of relativity. The theory the committee looked past reached a Nobel podium after all, carried there by the man the prize had honoured.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1919年5月29日，一次全**日食**(eclipse)**遮蔽了**(obscured)太阳，两支英国**考察队**(expeditions)拍摄了天空中看似位于太阳**附近**(vicinity)的恒星。阿瑟·爱丁顿**观测**(observed)于普林西比岛，这是一座岛，位于西非外海；克罗姆林和戴维森则在索布拉尔，位于巴西东北部。他们要检验**广义相对论**(general relativity)的一个**大胆的**(bold)预言，也就是太阳的**引力**(gravity)会使经过它附近的星光**偏折**(deflect)。

11月6日，英国皇家学会与皇家天文学会召开**联席**(joint)会议，观测**结果**(findings)被**盛赞为**(hailed as)证实了这一预言。《泰晤士报》**宣告了**(proclaimed)一场“科学革命”；《纽约时报》的**标题**(headline)写着“天上的光全歪了”。几乎**一夜之间**(overnight)，在**物理学家**(physicists)中**卓越的**(eminent)爱因斯坦成了举世皆知的**名人**(celebrity)。

斯德哥尔摩却没那么容易被**眩惑**(dazzle)。诺贝尔物理学委员会看重的是**严格的**(rigorous)**实验**(experimental)**证实**(confirmation)，而**委员会**(committee)成员阿尔瓦·古尔斯特兰德，一位获得过诺贝尔奖的眼科**专家**(specialist)，**认定**(deemed)相对论的**实证**(empirical)支持**不足**(insufficient)。由于没有一项**提名**(nomination)**符合**(fulfilled)诺贝尔定下的**标准**(criteria)，1921年的奖被**保留**(reserved)一年，这是**章程**(statutes)所**允许**(permit)的。

1922年11月9日，瑞典皇家科学院把这个奖**授予**(conferred on)爱因斯坦，**表彰**(citing)他对理论物理学的贡献，尤其是他发现了光电效应定律。这条定律**决定了**(governs)光如何把**电子**(electrons)从金属中**打出**(ejects)，曾帮助**奠定**(underpin)**量子**(quantum)理论的基础。第二天的一封信**澄清**(clarified)，此奖**并未考虑**(took no account of)相对论。爱因斯坦当时正**乘**(aboard)一艘**开往**(bound for)日本的**轮船**(steamer)，将错过12月的颁奖**典礼**(ceremony)。

1923年7月11日，在瑞典哥德堡，他**发表了**(delivered)他的诺贝尔**演讲**(lecture)，面向北欧自然科学家**大会**(congress)，**专门**(devoting to)讲相对论的**基本**(fundamental)思想与问题。委员会绕开不看的那个理论，终究登上了诺贝尔的**讲台**(podium)，把它带上去的，正是这个奖所**嘉奖**(honoured)的爱因斯坦。

approved_summary: 1919年日食观测被誉为证实太阳引力会使星光偏折，这一相对论预言让爱因斯坦迅速举世闻名。

1922年，保留的1921年度物理学奖授予爱因斯坦，表彰理论物理贡献，尤其是发现光电效应定律。
光电效应指光使金属释放电子，这一定律帮助奠定量子理论基础；授奖决定次日的信件明确：该奖不考虑相对论。
爱因斯坦赴日错过颁奖典礼；1923年，他的诺贝尔演讲却专讲相对论，让被奖项绕开的理论登上讲台。
